topic: The 'puff' eye pressure test: what it checks (glaucoma screening)

youtube.title: That puff of air at the eye test? 💨 Here's what it checks #Shorts
youtube.description:
That puff of air during an eye test: what does it actually check?
கண் பரிசோதனையில் காற்று ஊதும் சோதனை எதற்கு? கண் அழுத்தம்!

• The 'puff' test measures the pressure inside your eye; painless, and nothing touches your eye
• Your eye makes and drains a clear fluid; if it drains too slowly, pressure can harm the optic nerve
• Raised pressure is linked to glaucoma, which often has no pain and no early signs
• Lost side vision from glaucoma cannot be brought back, so early checks matter
• Higher risk: over 40, family history, diabetes, high short sight
• Urgent: sudden severe eye pain, red eye, headache with vomiting or halos around lights

gmb.text: The puff of air during an eye test measures the pressure inside your eye. It is painless and nothing touches the eye. Your eye constantly makes and drains a clear fluid; if it drains too slowly, pressure can build up and damage the optic nerve. This is linked to glaucoma, which often has no pain and no early warning signs, and lost side vision cannot be brought back. Pressure is one part of glaucoma screening, along with checking the optic nerve. Your risk is higher if you are over 40, have a parent or sibling with glaucoma, have diabetes or high short sight. See an eye specialist urgently for sudden severe eye pain, a red eye, headache with vomiting or rainbow halos around lights. Book an eye test on WhatsApp: 044 4356 9998
